title: Projected cost bound for the run
statement: Let an input consist of a positive dimension $n$, positive integers $a,d$ with $2a\le d$, and a Fourier bound $B\ge1$, and let the target be a function from the $n$-dimensional sign cube to the signs. Suppose a map from learning costs to nonnegative integers sends zero to zero and preserves addition. If, for some natural number $S$, the projection of the controller cost plus the stage cost is at most $S$ at every stage with index $k<n$ and active-set size at most the threshold's active cap, then for every $k\le n$ the projected cost of running the program through $k$ stages is at most $kS$.
hypotheses_covered: Valid deterministic Goldreich–Levin input, including positive dimension, accuracy bounds, and Fourier bound at least one
Target Boolean function on the sign cube
Cost projection sends zero to zero
Every eligible stage cost projection is at most the stage bound
